info.title: OpenAsy Helpdesk API
info.summary: Emails, forms and chats become tickets in queues, with owners, SLAs, replies from the support address and the customer from CRM.
info.description:
Every screen of Helpdesk uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Forms, Live Chat and a site's own form open tickets with `POST /api/v1/public/tickets`, with a source's key or from a page on its origins. Customers answer the satisfaction question at `/r/<token>`. Queues, routing rules, SLAs and the links to CRM and Knowledge Base come from the settings file, never the API. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

CRM is asked about a ticket's customer with `GET <crm.url>/api/v1/lookup?email=`; its answer is described here as `CrmLookup`.

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

200.description: The process is running.
The database answers and the settings are applied.

503.description: Not ready: the database or the settings are not there.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text format.
This product and its version.
From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.
Open and waiting tickets, by queue, and the SLAs about to run out: under an hour left, or missed.
As applied. No route changes it.
Who tickets can be given to.
Each address: whether it is read and sent from, the last reading and its error; the outbox; emails that did not become tickets, and why.

post.description:
Reads every address's new mail now instead of at its turn, and sends what is due in the outbox.

Needs the admin role.

200.description: Every address read, and the outbox sent.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A number (#1001), or words in the subject, the customer's name or address.

200.description: The SLA that runs out first first; paused and no-SLA tickets last.
How many changed hands.
With its thread, clocks and the saved answers for its queue.

patch.summary: Change owner, priority, queue or status
patch.description:
Solving stops the clocks and, after satisfaction.ask_after_solved, the customer is asked how it went. Waiting pauses them; open runs them again.

Needs the editor role.

200.description: The ticket after the change.

post.description:
Sent from the ticket's support address with a Message-ID of ours, In-Reply-To the customer's last email and References to the thread, and the ticket's number in the subject or reply address (mail.reply_token). Stops the first-reply clock; the ticket then waits on the customer unless status says otherwise. 409 when there is no customer email or no SMTP server.

Needs the editor role.

201.description: The reply, sent or waiting in the outbox to be tried again.
The note. Only the team sees it; no clock changes.

200.description: Matched by email only.
Up to three, for the ticket's subject. linked is false when the settings file links no Knowledge Base.
The file. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images are shown inline; anything else is downloaded as application/octet-stream, in a sandbox.
Tickets opened in the period, times in working hours, SLAs met and missed, and satisfaction, by queue and channel.

post.summary: A ticket from Forms, Live Chat or a site's form
post.description: Servers (Forms, Live Chat) send the source's key from the settings file as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Pages on one of the source's `origins` may post from the browser with no key (CORS), up to 10 a minute from one address; a browser cannot send agents' chat lines. Plain HTML forms may post `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, with other answers as `fields[<name>]`; they get a thank-you page, or a redirect.

200.description: The same external_id from the same source: the ticket it opened before.

201.description: Opened. HTML forms get a thank-you page.

202.description: Taken and dropped: the hidden website field was filled.

303.description: An HTML form with redirect: to that address.

post.summary: More of a chat, on its ticket
post.description: For the source that opened the ticket, with its key. A customer's line opens a waiting ticket again; an agent's line meets the first-reply clock.

get.description: The page the satisfaction email links to, with the answer from the link chosen. Nothing is kept until it is sent, so mail scanners that open links change nothing. In English, German or Turkish, from Accept-Language.

200.description: The question.

404.description: The link ended: 30 days after it was asked.

200.description: Thanks; or the question again when no score was chosen.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Helpdesk runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Helpdesk origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings, API tokens (`oa_helpdesk_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Helpdesk is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

sourceKey.description: The key of a source in the settings file (`sources.<id>.key` names the environment variable that holds it). Forms and Live Chat send it from their servers.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

anyOf.description: The settings file and whether it is applied; null before it was first read.

remaining.description: Working time left, ms; below zero once missed.

anyOf.description: The clock that matters now: the first reply until it is sent, then the solution. null when the queue sets no target, and for solved tickets.
One SLA clock, in ms of working time in the queue's hours; null when the queue sets no target for it.

body.description: Plain text: the new part of an email, without what it quoted.

anyOf.description: The whole email, with what it quoted, when that differs.
An email's HTML, sanitized: safe to show.
For system lines: opened, follows, crm-unavailable, reopened, moved, assigned, priority, status, solved, satisfaction-asked, satisfaction, acknowledged, auto-reply, bounce, delivery-failed.

TicketDetail.description: A ticket with its thread, clocks and saved answers.

anyOf.description: The support address replies go out from.

canReply.description: There is a customer email, and the address has an SMTP server.

source.description: The support address it came to, or the source id for forms and chats.

routedBy.description: Why it is in its queue, such as subject has "invoice".

anyOf.description: The customer's plan from CRM when the ticket was opened.

text.description: Filled for this ticket and the person asking.

anyOf.description: A member's id, or null for nobody.

queue.description: A queue id from the settings file. The clocks not met or missed start again with its SLA.

status.description: What the ticket is after the reply.

Customer.description: The customer from CRM, matched by email only. `linked: false` when the settings file links no CRM; the UI then shows nothing.

CrmLookup.description: What Helpdesk expects CRM to answer to GET <crm.url>/api/v1/lookup?email=<address> with Authorization: Bearer <key>: 200 with this, or 404 when no contact has exactly that address. Not a route of Helpdesk.

arrivals.description: Tickets a week on average, by weekday (Monday first) and hour, in the support's time zone.

anyOf.description: As the file sets it. Secrets are not in it: only the names of the environment variables holding them.

source.description: The source id from the settings file. With a key it may be left out: the key says which source it is.

email.description: The customer's address; replies go to it, and CRM is asked about it. Required for forms.

message.description: What the customer wrote. Required for forms without a transcript.

form.description: Which form, for routing rules with match.form.

fields.description: The form's other answers, shown with the message.

external_id.description: What Forms or Live Chat calls this request: the same id from the same source opens one ticket.

transcript.description: A chat's lines. Agents' lines need the source's key; with one, the first-reply clock is met.

website.description: Leave empty: a hidden field that only bots fill.

redirect.description: For HTML forms: where to send the browser after, on one of the source's origins; ?ticket=<number> is added.
